text: Hi! I'm Vari. I help people answer one kind of question.
speak: Hi! I'm Vari. I help people answer one kind of question.

text: Does this *cause* that?
speak: Does this cause that?

text: Does coffee make you work faster? Do ads raise sales? Does a new metro line cut traffic?
speak: Does coffee make you work faster? Do ads raise sales? Does a new metro line cut traffic?

text: Here's the trouble. We only ever see one version of the world.
speak: Here's the trouble. We only ever see one version of the world.

text: To learn the effect, we need a stand-in for the world we didn't get to see.
speak: To learn the effect, we need a stand-in for the world we didn't get to see.

text: So we hunt for *variation*: differences in the cause that are as fair as a coin flip.
speak: So we hunt for variation: differences in the cause that are as fair as a coin flip.

text: This is a field guide to the book *The Effect*, by Nick Huntington-Klein.
speak: This is a field guide to the book The Effect, by Nick Huntington-Klein.

text: First, how to *think* about a causal question. Then a toolbox of designs, each with two cases for you to try.
speak: First, how to think about a causal question. Then a toolbox of designs, each with two cases for you to try.

text: When I stop, pause and think. Tap Continue when you're ready.
speak: When I stop, pause and think. Tap Continue when you're ready.

text: The book has two halves.
speak: The book has two halves.

text: Part one is about thinking: designing research before touching any data.
speak: Part one is about thinking: designing research before touching any data.

text: Ask a sharp question.
speak: Ask a sharp question.

text: Describe your variables, and how they move together.
speak: Describe your variables, and how they move together.

text: Identify: draw the causal diagram, and find which comparisons answer your question.
speak: Identify: draw the causal diagram, and find which comparisons answer your question.

text: Interpret: know which average effect you've found, and test your assumptions.
speak: Interpret: know which average effect you've found, and test your assumptions.

text: Part two is the toolbox: templates that put a design to work on real data.
speak: Part two is the toolbox: templates that put a design to work on real data.

text: Control for back doors with regression or matching.
speak: Control for back doors with regression or matching.

text: Check any method with simulation.
speak: Check any method with simulation.

text: Use change over time: fixed effects, event studies, and difference-in-differences.
speak: Use change over time: fixed effects, event studies, and difference-in-differences.

text: Use an outside push: instrumental variables.
speak: Use an outside push: instrumental variables.

text: Use a rule's cutoff: regression discontinuity.
speak: Use a rule's cutoff: regression discontinuity.

text: Or settle for an honest range: partial identification.
speak: Or settle for an honest range: partial identification.

text: Then a few more methods, and the problems every study sweeps under the rug.
speak: Then a few more methods, and the problems every study sweeps under the rug.

text: Chapter one: design comes before data. Start with a question you could actually answer.
speak: Chapter one: design comes before data. Start with a question you could actually answer.

text: 'Does social media hurt sleep?' is too fuzzy. Hurt how? Whose sleep? Compared to what?
speak: 'Does social media hurt sleep?' is too fuzzy. Hurt how? Whose sleep? Compared to what?

text: Sharper: does an extra hour of Instagram after ten p.m. cut a teen's sleep that night?
speak: Sharper: does an extra hour of Instagram after ten p.m. cut a teen's sleep that night?

text: Now you know exactly what data you need, and what comparison would answer it.
speak: Now you know exactly what data you need, and what comparison would answer it.

text: Chapters three and four: describe before you explain.
speak: Chapters three and four: describe before you explain.

text: Here are a thousand Bengaluru commutes. Most take thirty to fifty minutes, with a long tail of two-hour slogs.
speak: Here are a thousand Bengaluru commutes. Most take thirty to fifty minutes, with a long tail of two-hour slogs.

text: The tail drags the mean up to fifty-two minutes. The median, forty-four, barely moves.
speak: The tail drags the mean up to fifty-two minutes. The median, forty-four, barely moves.

text: So look at the whole shape, not just one number.
speak: So look at the whole shape, not just one number.

text: Relationships too. On rainier days, the average commute climbs.
speak: Relationships too. On rainier days, the average commute climbs.

text: That's a conditional mean: the average commute *given* the rain. It isn't a cause yet.
speak: That's a conditional mean: the average commute given the rain. It isn't a cause yet.

text: Rainy days might also be school days or festival days. Describing comes first; explaining comes next.
speak: Rainy days might also be school days or festival days. Describing comes first; explaining comes next.

text: Chapter five: identification.
speak: Chapter five: identification.

text: Ice cream sales and drownings rise and fall together. Does ice cream drown people?
speak: Ice cream sales and drownings rise and fall together. Does ice cream drown people?

text: No. Summer heat drives both.
speak: No. Summer heat drives both.

text: Identification means finding the variation in ice cream sales that heat *can't* explain, and seeing whether drownings follow it.
speak: Identification means finding the variation in ice cream sales that heat can't explain, and seeing whether drownings follow it.

text: For example, compare days with the same temperature but different ice-cream deals. If drownings don't budge, ice cream is off the hook.
speak: For example, compare days with the same temperature but different ice-cream deals. If drownings don't budge, ice cream is off the hook.

text: Every design in this book is a way of finding that clean slice of variation.
speak: Every design in this book is a way of finding that clean slice of variation.

text: Chapters six and seven: causal diagrams. A picture of what causes what.
speak: Chapters six and seven: causal diagrams. A picture of what causes what.

text: Say we ask: does coffee raise how much you get done? Put the cause and the outcome on the page.
speak: Say we ask: does coffee raise how much you get done? Put the cause and the outcome on the page.

text: Then everything that could push either one. Poor sleep makes you drink coffee, and also slows you down.
speak: Then everything that could push either one. Poor sleep makes you drink coffee, and also slows you down.

text: A deadline makes you reach for coffee, and also makes you work harder.
speak: A deadline makes you reach for coffee, and also makes you work harder.

text: Stress matters too, but we can't measure it, so it gets a dashed circle.
speak: Stress matters too, but we can't measure it, so it gets a dashed circle.

text: Leave out what doesn't matter. Shoe size can go.
speak: Leave out what doesn't matter. Shoe size can go.

text: Every arrow, and every missing arrow, is an assumption you should be able to defend.
speak: Every arrow, and every missing arrow, is an assumption you should be able to defend.

text: Chapter eight: paths. Any route between coffee and output is a path.
speak: Chapter eight: paths. Any route between coffee and output is a path.

text: The direct arrow is a front door: it carries the effect we want.
speak: The direct arrow is a front door: it carries the effect we want.

text: Routes that begin with an arrow *into* coffee are back doors. Sleep and the deadline each open one.
speak: Routes that begin with an arrow into coffee are back doors. Sleep and the deadline each open one.

text: Back doors mix other causes into the comparison. Close one by controlling for the variable on it.
speak: Back doors mix other causes into the comparison. Close one by controlling for the variable on it.

text: Stress is unmeasured, so its door stays open. Part two is full of ways around that problem.
speak: Stress is unmeasured, so its door stays open. Part two is full of ways around that problem.

text: One trap: colliders. Among people in general, talent and good looks are unrelated.
speak: One trap: colliders. Among people in general, talent and good looks are unrelated.

text: But both help make someone famous. Look only at famous actors, and the talented ones seem plainer.
speak: But both help make someone famous. Look only at famous actors, and the talented ones seem plainer.

text: Fame is a collider. Controlling for it opens a path that was closed. So leave colliders alone.
speak: Fame is a collider. Controlling for it opens a path that was closed. So leave colliders alone.

text: Chapter nine: when you can't close a back door, find variation it can't reach.
speak: Chapter nine: when you can't close a back door, find variation it can't reach.

text: The cleanest way is to randomize. Flip a coin to decide who gets coffee.
speak: The cleanest way is to randomize. Flip a coin to decide who gets coffee.

text: Now sleep, deadlines and stress no longer point into coffee. Their back doors are cut.
speak: Now sleep, deadlines and stress no longer point into coffee. Their back doors are cut.

text: No experiment? Look for a natural experiment: a rule or an accident that did the coin-flipping for you.
speak: No experiment? Look for a natural experiment: a rule or an accident that did the coin-flipping for you.

text: Say the office coffee machine breaks on random days. Those days are your coin flips.
speak: Say the office coffee machine breaks on random days. Those days are your coin flips.

text: Or use the front-door method: if coffee works only through alertness, and nothing else touches alertness, trace the effect through it.
speak: Or use the front-door method: if coffee works only through alertness, and nothing else touches alertness, trace the effect through it.

text: Chapter ten: an effect isn't one number. It differs from person to person.
speak: Chapter ten: an effect isn't one number. It differs from person to person.

text: Take a fitness app's new streak feature. For some users it adds eight workouts a month; for others, none.
speak: Take a fitness app's new streak feature. For some users it adds eight workouts a month; for others, none.

text: Average it over everyone and you get the average treatment effect, the ATE: three extra workouts.
speak: Average it over everyone and you get the average treatment effect, the A.T.E.: three extra workouts.

text: Average over just the people who switched it on and you get the effect on the treated, the ATT: five. They chose it because it helps them.
speak: Average over just the people who switched it on and you get the effect on the treated, the A.T.T.: five. They chose it because it helps them.

text: Average over the people a random prompt nudged into using it, and you get the local average treatment effect, the LATE: about two point seven.
speak: Average over the people a random prompt nudged into using it, and you get the local average treatment effect, the L.A.T.E.: about two point seven.

text: Different designs recover different averages. Always ask: whose effect is this?
speak: Different designs recover different averages. Always ask: whose effect is this?

text: Chapter eleven: you'll never know the whole diagram. And you don't need to.
speak: Chapter eleven: you'll never know the whole diagram. And you don't need to.

text: Focus on what drives the treatment: the roads into it. That is where back doors begin.
speak: Focus on what drives the treatment: the roads into it. That is where back doors begin.

text: And test what you can. A placebo test checks for an effect that *should* be zero.
speak: And test what you can. A placebo test checks for an effect that should be zero.

text: Coffee today can't change yesterday's output. If it seems to, something else is going on.
speak: Coffee today can't change yesterday's output. If it seems to, something else is going on.

text: Passing a placebo test doesn't prove you're right. Failing one tells you something is wrong.
speak: Passing a placebo test doesn't prove you're right. Failing one tells you something is wrong.

text: Part one leaves you here: a diagram with back doors. Some you can measure and close. Some you can't.
speak: Part one leaves you here: a diagram with back doors. Some you can measure and close. Some you can't.

text: Part two is a set of templates for dealing with them. And they all answer one question.
speak: Part two is a set of templates for dealing with them. And they all answer one question.

text: Which part of the variation in the treatment do we keep?
speak: Which part of the variation in the treatment do we keep?

text: Every design keeps a different slice, and throws away the slices that back doors can reach.
speak: Every design keeps a different slice, and throws away the slices that back doors can reach.

text: Group them, and five families appear.
speak: Group them, and five families appear.

text: One: measure the back doors and hold them fixed. Regression and matching. This works if you can see every confounder.
speak: One: measure the back doors and hold them fixed. Regression and matching. This works if you can see every confounder.

text: Two: compare a unit with itself over time, or with a group that shares its trend. Fixed effects, event studies, and difference-in-differences.
speak: Two: compare a unit with itself over time, or with a group that shares its trend. Fixed effects, event studies, and difference-in-differences.

text: Three: find an outside push that moves the treatment. Instrumental variables.
speak: Three: find an outside push that moves the treatment. Instrumental variables.

text: Four: use a rule's edge, where a cutoff decides who's treated. Regression discontinuity.
speak: Four: use a rule's edge, where a cutoff decides who's treated. Regression discontinuity.

text: Five: when nothing gives a clean slice, report a range. Partial identification.
speak: Five: when nothing gives a clean slice, report a range. Partial identification.

text: And simulation is the test bench: build a fake world with a known answer, and check any of them.
speak: And simulation is the test bench: build a fake world with a known answer, and check any of them.

text: Why does this short list cover so much ground? Because a back door can only be handled in a few ways.
speak: Why does this short list cover so much ground? Because a back door can only be handled in a few ways.

text: You can see it and control it. It can stay fixed, or be shared, so comparisons within cancel it. Or you can route around it, with an outside push or a rule.
speak: You can see it and control it. It can stay fixed, or be shared, so comparisons within cancel it. Or you can route around it, with an outside push or a rule.

text: If none of those hold, you bound the answer. So choosing a design is a short flowchart.
speak: If none of those hold, you bound the answer. So choosing a design is a short flowchart.

text: Randomize if you can.
speak: Randomize if you can.

text: If not: can you measure every back door?
speak: If not: can you measure every back door?

text: Do you see the same units over time?
speak: Do you see the same units over time?

text: Is there a start date, and a group it missed?
speak: Is there a start date, and a group it missed?

text: Is there an outside push?
speak: Is there an outside push?

text: Or a cutoff?
speak: Or a cutoff?

text: If nothing fits, report a range.
speak: If nothing fits, report a range.

text: The designs also combine.
speak: The designs also combine.

text: Difference-in-differences is fixed effects for both groups and time.
speak: Difference-in-differences is fixed effects for both groups and time.

text: A fuzzy cutoff turns regression discontinuity into an instrument.
speak: A fuzzy cutoff turns regression discontinuity into an instrument.

text: And matching can build a better comparison group for difference-in-differences.
speak: And matching can build a better comparison group for difference-in-differences.

text: It isn't the whole story. Synthetic control, structural models and more wait in the gallery near the end.
speak: It isn't the whole story. Synthetic control, structural models and more wait in the gallery near the end.

text: Now, each design, one at a time. Two cases each. Ready?
speak: Now, each design, one at a time. Two cases each. Ready?

text: Regression. Let's start with the name.
speak: Regression. Let's start with the name.

text: Francis Galton noticed that tall parents' children tended to 'go back', or regress, toward average height. The line-fitting tool that showed it kept the name.
speak: Francis Galton noticed that tall parents' children tended to 'go back', or regress, toward average height. The line-fitting tool that showed it kept the name.

text: Regression fits a line through the data, so you can compare outcomes across the treatment *while holding measured controls fixed*.
speak: Regression fits a line through the data, so you can compare outcomes across the treatment while holding measured controls fixed.

text: Picture a line through the cloud of data, and a lock on every control.
speak: Picture a line through the cloud of data, and a lock on every control.

text: Use it when:
speak: Use it when:

text: You can name and measure every back-door variable
speak: You can name and measure every back-door variable

text: The outcome changes in a shape you can model, like a line
speak: The outcome changes in a shape you can model, like a line

text: Treated and untreated units overlap on those controls
speak: Treated and untreated units overlap on those controls

text: Case 1. Chai stalls near metro stations sell ₹1,500 more a day. But those stalls also sit on busier roads. How would you estimate what the metro itself adds?
speak: Case 1. Chai stalls near metro stations sell 1,500 rupees more a day. But those stalls also sit on busier roads. How would you estimate what the metro itself adds?

text: Regress daily sales on 'near a metro', and add the road's foot traffic as a control.
speak: Regress daily sales on 'near a metro', and add the road's foot traffic as a control.

text: The control means we compare stalls with the *same* foot traffic, near a station and far from one.
speak: The control means we compare stalls with the same foot traffic, near a station and far from one.

text: The raw gap of ₹1,500 shrinks to ₹500. That's the metro's effect, if foot traffic was the only back door.
speak: The raw gap of 1,500 rupees shrinks to 500 rupees. That's the metro's effect, if foot traffic was the only back door.

text: Case 2. Students who sleep more score higher. But they also study less late at night, and fewer have part-time jobs. How would regression help, and what could still go wrong?
speak: Case 2. Students who sleep more score higher. But they also study less late at night, and fewer have part-time jobs. How would regression help, and what could still go wrong?

text: Regress exam score on hours of sleep, controlling for late-night study and job hours.
speak: Regress exam score on hours of sleep, controlling for late-night study and job hours.

text: Each control closes one back door. The sleep slope now compares students who are alike on both.
speak: Each control closes one back door. The sleep slope now compares students who are alike on both.

text: But stress, which we didn't measure, still drives both sleep and scores. Regression is only as good as its list of controls.
speak: But stress, which we didn't measure, still drives both sleep and scores. Regression is only as good as its list of controls.

text: Regression closes the back doors you can measure. The ones you can't, stay open.
speak: Regression closes the back doors you can measure. The ones you can't, stay open.

text: Matching. The name says exactly what it does.
speak: Matching. The name says exactly what it does.

text: Like pairing socks from the laundry. For every treated unit, find an untreated one that looks the same on the back-door variables.
speak: Like pairing socks from the laundry. For every treated unit, find an untreated one that looks the same on the back-door variables.

text: Matching pairs each treated unit with untreated look-alikes on the measured back-door variables, then compares outcomes within those pairs.
speak: Matching pairs each treated unit with untreated look-alikes on the measured back-door variables, then compares outcomes within those pairs.

text: Picture two columns of people, joined into pairs. Anyone without a twin sits out.
speak: Picture two columns of people, joined into pairs. Anyone without a twin sits out.

text: Treated and untreated groups differ on traits you can measure
speak: Treated and untreated groups differ on traits you can measure

text: Look-alikes exist on both sides (they overlap)
speak: Look-alikes exist on both sides (they overlap)

text: You'd rather not assume a straight-line relationship
speak: You'd rather not assume a straight-line relationship

text: Case 1. A gym offers free personal training to members who ask. Trainer users lose more weight, but they tend to be younger and newer members. How would you use matching?
speak: Case 1. A gym offers free personal training to members who ask. Trainer users lose more weight, but they tend to be younger and newer members. How would you use matching?

text: Pair each trainer user with a non-user of the same age and the same months of membership.
speak: Pair each trainer user with a non-user of the same age and the same months of membership.

text: Compare weight change within each pair, then average across the pairs.
speak: Compare weight change within each pair, then average across the pairs.

text: Members with no look-alike are dropped. You learn the effect for users who have a fair comparison.
speak: Members with no look-alike are dropped. You learn the effect for users who have a fair comparison.

text: Case 2. Did a coding bootcamp raise graduates' salaries? Attendees had more work experience and more often lived in Bengaluru. How would you set up the comparison?
speak: Case 2. Did a coding bootcamp raise graduates' salaries? Attendees had more work experience and more often lived in Bengaluru. How would you set up the comparison?

text: Match each graduate to non-attendees with the same experience, city, degree and starting salary. Now the groups are balanced.
speak: Match each graduate to non-attendees with the same experience, city, degree and starting salary. Now the groups are balanced.

text: Then compare salary growth: graduates grew twenty-two percent, their matches fourteen.
speak: Then compare salary growth: graduates grew twenty-two percent, their matches fourteen.

text: Careful: motivation isn't on the list. If keener people enrol, matching can't fix that.
speak: Careful: motivation isn't on the list. If keener people enrol, matching can't fix that.

text: Matching compares like with like, but only on the traits you can see.
speak: Matching compares like with like, but only on the traits you can see.

text: Simulation. To simulate is to imitate.
speak: Simulation. To simulate is to imitate.

text: You build a pretend world on a computer, where *you* choose the true effect.
speak: You build a pretend world on a computer, where you choose the true effect.

text: Simulation creates many fake datasets with a known true effect, runs your method on each one, and checks whether it gets the truth back.
speak: Simulation creates many fake datasets with a known true effect, runs your method on each one, and checks whether it gets the truth back.

text: Picture a dial set to the truth, a stack of fake datasets, and a pile of estimates around the dial.
speak: Picture a dial set to the truth, a stack of fake datasets, and a pile of estimates around the dial.

text: You want to test a method before you trust it
speak: You want to test a method before you trust it

text: The sample is small, or the design is complicated
speak: The sample is small, or the design is complicated

text: You suspect a control or an assumption could bias the answer
speak: You suspect a control or an assumption could bias the answer

text: Case 1. You plan to measure a discount's effect on sales, but you only have 30 stores. Will your estimate be precise enough to trust?
speak: Case 1. You plan to measure a discount's effect on sales, but you only have 30 stores. Will your estimate be precise enough to trust?

text: Build a fake world: thirty stores, a true effect of plus five percent, and realistic noise.
speak: Build a fake world: thirty stores, a true effect of plus five percent, and realistic noise.

text: Run your analysis on a thousand fake versions. The estimates land anywhere from minus three to plus thirteen percent.
speak: Run your analysis on a thousand fake versions. The estimates land anywhere from minus three to plus thirteen percent.

text: Far too noisy. Before spending money, you know you need more stores.
speak: Far too noisy. Before spending money, you know you need more stores.

text: Case 2. A colleague wants to control for customer satisfaction when estimating how delivery speed affects repeat orders. Is that safe?
speak: Case 2. A colleague wants to control for customer satisfaction when estimating how delivery speed affects repeat orders. Is that safe?

text: Simulate a world where speed raises satisfaction, and satisfaction drives repeat orders. Set the true effect of speed at ten.
speak: Simulate a world where speed raises satisfaction, and satisfaction drives repeat orders. Set the true effect of speed at ten.

text: Without the control, the estimates centre on ten. With it, they centre near two.
speak: Without the control, the estimates centre on ten. With it, they centre near two.

text: Satisfaction sits on the path from speed to orders, so controlling for it hides most of the effect. The simulation caught the mistake before it was published.
speak: Satisfaction sits on the path from speed to orders, so controlling for it hides most of the effect. The simulation caught the mistake before it was published.

text: When you know the answer, you can test the method.
speak: When you know the answer, you can test the method.

text: Fixed effects. Two words, and both matter.
speak: Fixed effects. Two words, and both matter.

text: 'Fixed' means traits of each unit that stay put over time, like a player's talent or a shop's location.
speak: 'Fixed' means traits of each unit that stay put over time, like a player's talent or a shop's location.

text: 'Effects' means the push those traits give the outcome. The design wipes out every fixed effect by comparing each unit only with itself.
speak: 'Effects' means the push those traits give the outcome. The design wipes out every fixed effect by comparing each unit only with itself.

text: Fixed effects compare each unit with itself at different times, so everything about it that never changes drops out.
speak: Fixed effects compare each unit with itself at different times, so everything about it that never changes drops out.

text: Picture three units at different heights. Slide each one to the same level, and only the change within each is left.
speak: Picture three units at different heights. Slide each one to the same level, and only the change within each is left.

text: You observe the same units again and again (panel data)
speak: You observe the same units again and again (panel data)

text: The worrying back doors are stable traits of each unit
speak: The worrying back doors are stable traits of each unit

text: Treatment switches on and off within units over time
speak: Treatment switches on and off within units over time

text: Case 1. Do cricketers score more runs in matches where they use a new bat? Better players are more likely to get the new bat first. How do you get a fair answer?
speak: Case 1. Do cricketers score more runs in matches where they use a new bat? Better players are more likely to get the new bat first. How do you get a fair answer?

text: Pooled together, new-bat innings average fifty-two runs and old-bat innings twenty-five. But stars dominate the new-bat column.
speak: Pooled together, new-bat innings average fifty-two runs and old-bat innings twenty-five. But stars dominate the new-bat column.

text: So compare each player's new-bat runs with *their own* old-bat runs. Talent is fixed, so it cancels out.
speak: So compare each player's new-bat runs with their own old-bat runs. Talent is fixed, so it cancels out.

text: Each player gains about six runs. That's the bat. But anything that changes over time, like form or fitness, could still sneak in.
speak: Each player gains about six runs. That's the bat. But anything that changes over time, like form or fitness, could still sneak in.

text: Case 2. Restaurants get better ratings in months when they're listed on a delivery app. But fancier restaurants join apps more often. How would fixed effects help?
speak: Case 2. Restaurants get better ratings in months when they're listed on a delivery app. But fancier restaurants join apps more often. How would fixed effects help?

text: Use restaurant fixed effects: compare each restaurant's ratings in its app months with its own months off the app.
speak: Use restaurant fixed effects: compare each restaurant's ratings in its app months with its own months off the app.

text: Fanciness, location and cuisine don't change month to month, so they drop out. Each restaurant gains about point two stars.
speak: Fanciness, location and cuisine don't change month to month, so they drop out. Each restaurant gains about point two stars.

text: A new chef or a renovation *does* change, so check for those separately.
speak: A new chef or a renovation does change, so check for those separately.

text: Compare each unit with itself, and whatever never changes about it disappears.
speak: Compare each unit with itself, and whatever never changes about it disappears.

text: Event studies.
speak: Event studies.

text: The 'event' is the moment a treatment switches on.
speak: The 'event' is the moment a treatment switches on.

text: The 'study' tracks the outcome before and after that moment.
speak: The 'study' tracks the outcome before and after that moment.

text: An event study compares what happens after a treatment starts with what the trend before it predicted would happen.
speak: An event study compares what happens after a treatment starts with what the trend before it predicted would happen.

text: Picture the trend before the event, extended forward as a forecast. The gap after the event is the effect.
speak: Picture the trend before the event, extended forward as a forecast. The gap after the event is the effect.

text: There is a clear date when the treatment begins
speak: There is a clear date when the treatment begins

text: You have data well before and well after that date
speak: You have data well before and well after that date

text: Nothing else big changes at the same moment
speak: Nothing else big changes at the same moment

text: Case 1. A new metro line opens on 1 March, running right beside a busy bus route. Did ridership on that bus route fall?
speak: Case 1. A new metro line opens on 1 March, running right beside a busy bus route. Did ridership on that bus route fall?

text: Plot weekly bus riders for months before and after the opening.
speak: Plot weekly bus riders for months before and after the opening.

text: Fit the trend before March, and extend it forward as a forecast of a world with no metro.
speak: Fit the trend before March, and extend it forward as a forecast of a world with no metro.

text: The gap between the forecast and actual riders, about four thousand a week, is the effect. And before March, the estimated effect hovers at zero, as it should.
speak: The gap between the forecast and actual riders, about four thousand a week, is the effect. And before March, the estimated effect hovers at zero, as it should.

text: Case 2. A shopping app launched a redesign on one day in October, and daily orders went up. Was it the redesign?
speak: Case 2. A shopping app launched a redesign on one day in October, and daily orders went up. Was it the redesign?

text: Line up daily orders around launch day, and compare them with the trend before launch.
speak: Line up daily orders around launch day, and compare them with the trend before launch.

text: But October brings festival sales. If Diwali offers began the same week, an event study can't tell the two apart.
speak: But October brings festival sales. If Diwali offers began the same week, an event study can't tell the two apart.

text: Use a narrow window around the launch, and check what else changed that day. A clean event date is everything.
speak: Use a narrow window around the launch, and check what else changed that day. A clean event date is everything.

text: Before-and-after works when the trend is predictable and nothing else changed.
speak: Before-and-after works when the trend is predictable and nothing else changed.

text: Difference-in-differences. The name is the recipe.
speak: Difference-in-differences. The name is the recipe.

text: The first difference: after minus before, within each group.
speak: The first difference: after minus before, within each group.

text: The second: the treated group's change minus the untreated group's change. That subtracts whatever changed for everyone.
speak: The second: the treated group's change minus the untreated group's change. That subtracts whatever changed for everyone.

text: Difference-in-differences compares how much a treated group changed with how much a similar untreated group changed over the same period.
speak: Difference-in-differences compares how much a treated group changed with how much a similar untreated group changed over the same period.

text: Picture two lines moving together. After treatment, a ghost line shows where the treated group would have gone.
speak: Picture two lines moving together. After treatment, a ghost line shows where the treated group would have gone.

text: A treated and an untreated group, both seen before and after
speak: A treated and an untreated group, both seen before and after

text: Both groups were trending in parallel before treatment
speak: Both groups were trending in parallel before treatment

text: Nothing else hit only the treated group at the same time
speak: Nothing else hit only the treated group at the same time

text: Case 1. Karnataka raises the minimum wage for shop workers; a neighbouring state doesn't. Did shop jobs in Karnataka fall?
speak: Case 1. Karnataka raises the minimum wage for shop workers; a neighbouring state doesn't. Did shop jobs in Karnataka fall?

text: Measure Karnataka's change in shop jobs, before versus after. Do the same for the neighbouring state.
speak: Measure Karnataka's change in shop jobs, before versus after. Do the same for the neighbouring state.

text: Karnataka fell by two percent. The neighbour fell by three percent, for reasons that had nothing to do with wages.
speak: Karnataka fell by two percent. The neighbour fell by three percent, for reasons that had nothing to do with wages.

text: Difference in differences: minus two, minus minus three, gives plus one percent. No sign the wage rise cut jobs, if the two states were trending together.
speak: Difference in differences: minus two, minus minus three, gives plus one percent. No sign the wage rise cut jobs, if the two states were trending together.

text: Case 2. One school district bans phones in class from June; a nearby district does not. Test scores rise in both. Did the ban help?
speak: Case 2. One school district bans phones in class from June; a nearby district does not. Test scores rise in both. Did the ban help?

text: Compare the change in scores in the banning district with the change next door.
speak: Compare the change in scores in the banning district with the change next door.

text: Banning district: up eight points. Neighbour: up five. Difference in differences: three points.
speak: Banning district: up eight points. Neighbour: up five. Difference in differences: three points.

text: But first check earlier years. If the two districts moved in parallel before the ban, the neighbour is a fair stand-in.
speak: But first check earlier years. If the two districts moved in parallel before the ban, the neighbour is a fair stand-in.

text: The untreated group tells you what would have happened anyway.
speak: The untreated group tells you what would have happened anyway.

text: Instrumental variables.
speak: Instrumental variables.

text: An instrument is a tool: something outside the system that moves the treatment.
speak: An instrument is a tool: something outside the system that moves the treatment.

text: And a variable, because it's something we can measure.
speak: And a variable, because it's something we can measure.

text: An instrumental variable shifts the treatment but reaches the outcome only through the treatment, so we keep just the variation it creates.
speak: An instrumental variable shifts the treatment but reaches the outcome only through the treatment, so we keep just the variation it creates.

text: Picture a push, Z, on the treatment. Back doors still tangle X and Y, but the push has no other road to Y.
speak: Picture a push, Z, on the treatment. Back doors still tangle X and Y, but the push has no other road to Y.

text: The treatment is tangled with things you can't measure
speak: The treatment is tangled with things you can't measure

text: Some outside push changes who gets treated
speak: Some outside push changes who gets treated

text: That push has no other road to the outcome
speak: That push has no other road to the outcome

text: Case 1. Does a top coaching institute raise entrance-exam scores? Students who join are more motivated. But seats go by lottery among applicants. How can you use that?
speak: Case 1. Does a top coaching institute raise entrance-exam scores? Students who join are more motivated. But seats go by lottery among applicants. How can you use that?

text: The lottery is the instrument. It decides who gets a seat, and it can't know who's motivated.
speak: The lottery is the instrument. It decides who gets a seat, and it can't know who's motivated.

text: Lottery winners score three points higher on average. And winning raises the chance of joining by fifty percentage points.
speak: Lottery winners score three points higher on average. And winning raises the chance of joining by fifty percentage points.

text: Divide: three points over one half gives six points. That is the effect for students whose choice the lottery actually changed.
speak: Divide: three points over one half gives six points. That is the effect for students whose choice the lottery actually changed.

text: Case 2. Do people exercise more when they live near a park? Fitter people may choose park-side homes. A city housing scheme assigns flats by lottery. Where is the instrument?
speak: Case 2. Do people exercise more when they live near a park? Fitter people may choose park-side homes. A city housing scheme assigns flats by lottery. Where is the instrument?

text: The flat lottery. Some winners happen to land near a park, purely by chance.
speak: The flat lottery. Some winners happen to land near a park, purely by chance.

text: Use the lottery-assigned distance to a park as the instrument for actual distance.
speak: Use the lottery-assigned distance to a park as the instrument for actual distance.

text: It works only if the lottery changes exercise through the park alone. If park-side flats also came with a gym, the instrument would fail.
speak: It works only if the lottery changes exercise through the park alone. If park-side flats also came with a gym, the instrument would fail.

text: An instrument is a fair push from outside. Keep only the variation it moves.
speak: An instrument is a fair push from outside. Keep only the variation it moves.

text: Regression discontinuity.
speak: Regression discontinuity.

text: 'Regression': fit a line on each side of a cutoff.
speak: 'Regression': fit a line on each side of a cutoff.

text: 'Discontinuity': a sudden break in the line, right at the cutoff. The size of that jump is the effect.
speak: 'Discontinuity': a sudden break in the line, right at the cutoff. The size of that jump is the effect.

text: When a cutoff on some score decides who is treated, compare units just above and just below it. The jump at the cutoff is the effect.
speak: When a cutoff on some score decides who is treated, compare units just above and just below it. The jump at the cutoff is the effect.

text: Picture dots climbing smoothly, then a jump at the cutoff, where treatment switches on.
speak: Picture dots climbing smoothly, then a jump at the cutoff, where treatment switches on.

text: Treatment is assigned by a cutoff on a score
speak: Treatment is assigned by a cutoff on a score

text: People can't precisely control which side they land on
speak: People can't precisely control which side they land on

text: Nothing else changes at that exact cutoff
speak: Nothing else changes at that exact cutoff

text: Case 1. A scholarship goes to every student scoring 85 or more on a test. Does the scholarship raise college graduation?
speak: Case 1. A scholarship goes to every student scoring 85 or more on a test. Does the scholarship raise college graduation?

text: Plot graduation rates against test scores, and fit a line on each side of eighty-five.
speak: Plot graduation rates against test scores, and fit a line on each side of eighty-five.

text: Students at eighty-four and eighty-six are nearly identical, except one has the scholarship. The jump, nine points, is its effect.
speak: Students at eighty-four and eighty-six are nearly identical, except one has the scholarship. The jump, nine points, is its effect.

text: Then check for bunching. If students could nudge their scores over eighty-five, the comparison would break. Here, the counts are smooth.
speak: Then check for bunching. If students could nudge their scores over eighty-five, the comparison would break. Here, the counts are smooth.

text: Case 2. Shops with yearly turnover above ₹40 lakh must register for GST. Does registering cut profits? What would you check first?
speak: Case 2. Shops with yearly turnover above 40 lakh rupees must register for G.S.T.. Does registering cut profits? What would you check first?

text: The plan: compare the profits of shops just below and just above ₹40 lakh.
speak: The plan: compare the profits of shops just below and just above 40 lakh rupees.

text: But first, count the shops near the line. There's a pile-up just under it. Owners are keeping turnover low on purpose.
speak: But first, count the shops near the line. There's a pile-up just under it. Owners are keeping turnover low on purpose.

text: That's manipulation. Shops just below aren't like shops just above, so this cutoff won't give a clean answer.
speak: That's manipulation. Shops just below aren't like shops just above, so this cutoff won't give a clean answer.

text: Near a strict cutoff, chance decides the side. Unless people can game it.
speak: Near a strict cutoff, chance decides the side. Unless people can game it.

text: Partial identification.
speak: Partial identification.

text: 'Identification' means pinning down the effect from data plus assumptions. 'Partial' means you only pin down part of it.
speak: 'Identification' means pinning down the effect from data plus assumptions. 'Partial' means you only pin down part of it.

text: So instead of a single number, you get a range, and you can see what each assumption buys you.
speak: So instead of a single number, you get a range, and you can see what each assumption buys you.

text: Partial identification reports the range of effects that fit the data under weak assumptions, and shows how each extra assumption narrows it.
speak: Partial identification reports the range of effects that fit the data under weak assumptions, and shows how each extra assumption narrows it.

text: Picture a wide bar. Each assumption you add squeezes it tighter.
speak: Picture a wide bar. Each assumption you add squeezes it tighter.

text: Strong assumptions aren't believable
speak: Strong assumptions aren't believable

text: Data are missing, or selection can't be fixed
speak: Data are missing, or selection can't be fixed

text: An honest range is more useful than a shaky number
speak: An honest range is more useful than a shaky number

text: Case 1. A job-training program surveyed participants' wages, but thirty percent never replied. What can you honestly say about the program's effect on wages?
speak: Case 1. A job-training program surveyed participants' wages, but thirty percent never replied. What can you honestly say about the program's effect on wages?

text: Fill the gaps with the worst case and the best case: non-repliers earn the least possible, or the most.
speak: Fill the gaps with the worst case and the best case: non-repliers earn the least possible, or the most.

text: That gives a wide range. The effect is somewhere between minus ₹2,000 and plus ₹6,000 a month.
speak: That gives a wide range. The effect is somewhere between minus 2,000 rupees and plus 6,000 rupees a month.

text: Add one believable assumption, that non-repliers earn no more than repliers, and the range tightens to between zero and plus ₹3,000.
speak: Add one believable assumption, that non-repliers earn no more than repliers, and the range tightens to between zero and plus 3,000 rupees.

text: Case 2. A city adds a traffic signal, and reported accidents drop. But many minor accidents never get reported. Did the signal really reduce accidents?
speak: Case 2. A city adds a traffic signal, and reported accidents drop. But many minor accidents never get reported. Did the signal really reduce accidents?

text: We don't know how many accidents went unreported, before or after.
speak: We don't know how many accidents went unreported, before or after.

text: Assume only that reporting didn't *fall* after the signal went in. Then the true drop is at least as big as the reported drop.
speak: Assume only that reporting didn't fall after the signal went in. Then the true drop is at least as big as the reported drop.

text: That's a one-sided bound: the signal cut accidents by at least twelve percent. Honest, and still useful.
speak: That's a one-sided bound: the signal cut accidents by at least twelve percent. Honest, and still useful.

text: When certainty isn't available, an honest range beats a confident guess.
speak: When certainty isn't available, an honest range beats a confident guess.

text: Chapter twenty-two: a gallery of other methods. Three quick portraits.
speak: Chapter twenty-two: a gallery of other methods. Three quick portraits.

text: Synthetic control. When one city adopts a policy, blend several other cities into a stand-in that tracked it closely before.
speak: Synthetic control. When one city adopts a policy, blend several other cities into a stand-in that tracked it closely before.

text: After the policy, the gap between the city and its blend is the effect.
speak: After the policy, the gap between the city and its blend is the effect.

text: Heterogeneous effects. Instead of one average, let the data sort people into groups that respond differently. Maybe tutoring helps beginners the most.
speak: Heterogeneous effects. Instead of one average, let the data sort people into groups that respond differently. Maybe tutoring helps beginners the most.

text: Structural estimation. Write down a theory of how people decide, like how shoppers weigh price against distance, and fit it to data.
speak: Structural estimation. Write down a theory of how people decide, like how shoppers weigh price against distance, and fit it to data.

text: Then you can ask about policies nobody has tried yet.
speak: Then you can ask about policies nobody has tried yet.

text: Chapter twenty-three: every study sweeps something under the rug. Good researchers lift it and say what they found.
speak: Chapter twenty-three: every study sweeps something under the rug. Good researchers lift it and say what they found.

text: Which model? Two reasonable choices can give two different answers.
speak: Which model? Two reasonable choices can give two different answers.

text: Are you measuring the right thing? A test score is not quite the same as learning.
speak: Are you measuring the right thing? A test score is not quite the same as learning.

text: Missing data: who stopped answering, and why?
speak: Missing data: who stopped answering, and why?

text: Spillovers: tutoring one child can help her deskmate too, which muddies the comparison.
speak: Spillovers: tutoring one child can help her deskmate too, which muddies the comparison.

text: Fat tails: one billionaire in the sample can wreck an average.
speak: Fat tails: one billionaire in the sample can wreck an average.

text: And what exactly is the treatment? 'Tutoring' can mean many different things.
speak: And what exactly is the treatment? 'Tutoring' can mean many different things.

text: None of these sink a study by themselves. Hiding them does.
speak: None of these sink a study by themselves. Hiding them does.

text: So, every design in the book is a way to find a fair comparison.
speak: So, every design in the book is a way to find a fair comparison.

text: Part one tells you which comparisons would work. Part two gives you templates to make them. And honesty about the rug keeps you safe.
speak: Part one tells you which comparisons would work. Part two gives you templates to make them. And honesty about the rug keeps you safe.

text: Keep asking why. Thanks for exploring with me!
